# ConfigHub for Coding Agents (Door A)

> Build your app with Claude Code or Codex and keep it easy to change. Durable config for environments, previews, linked starters, and production approvals with no platform to build first.

Base URL: https://confighub.github.io/helm-expt/ai-agents/
Machine-readable catalog: https://confighub.github.io/helm-expt/ai-agents/catalog.json

## When to use this door vs Door B

- Use **Door A (`ai-agents/`)** when the user is building or deploying an app with Claude Code or Codex (envs, `.env` files, previews, Vercel, Fly, Unikraft, AWS SSM, Daytona, Stripe/Supabase/Resend add-ons, Kustomize Argo CD/Flux app starters, nono sandbox, or reusing working settings across apps).
- Use **Door B (`site/`)** when the user is working with Helm charts, full Kubernetes clusters, NVIDIA AICR, GPU fleets, Sveltos, Kubara, or multi-component cluster stacks:
  https://confighub.github.io/helm-expt/site/llms.txt
- Cross-door handoff: for an app using the Kubernetes Workshop Redis package, its Workshop catalog ID is `bitnami-redis-25-5-3-reuse-existing-secret` (`https://confighub.github.io/helm-expt/site/listings/bitnami-redis-25-5-3-reuse-existing-secret.json`), and the [Redis handoff](https://confighub.github.io/helm-expt/site/redis-walkthrough.html#local-to-shared) follows it into mini and a shared hub (mini Story 18.02). Workshop catalog IDs and mini story numbers identify different records.

## First after install

- Existing or partly built app: open `index.html#in-my-app`. Ask “What does ConfigHub remember about a setting we changed here, and why?” The record can be empty. Start it with one requested setting edit and its reason.
- Empty folder: open `index.html#build-my-first-app`. Ask for the app normally. For a runnable local example: “Build a small Node app for my neighborhood market. Give it a heading I can change in .env, run it locally and give me the link.”
- Five-minute sample: open `index.html#first-prompt`. Start with CACHE=off, change it for Saturday’s sale, then ask “Why is the cache on?” in a new chat.
- Kept preview: open `index.html#try-a-change-in-my-app`. For a direct-start Node web app, the agent can offer local setup, run the preview after consent and find it in a new chat in the same folder. With history on this hub, ask “Open Friday’s production settings as a new preview.” The current code runs with the saved settings.
- Reuse: open `first-look.html#starter` when the user asks for another app like the first. Introduce the shared hub when a colleague or CI needs access. An app request for Daytona uses the app starter; follow the Kubernetes door when the user actually wants cluster operations.

## Progression ladder

1. **Step 1: Plugin** (`plugin.html`)
   Install in Claude Code (`claude plugin marketplace add confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin && claude plugin install confighub@confighub`) or Codex CLI (`curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/install-codex.sh | bash`). MIT-licensed hooks, launcher, and starters wrapping a prebuilt local binary. Records why supported settings changed locally in `~/.confighub` (including a first-run 30-day Claude Code transcript read and pattern-based credential redaction). Zero background processes, no account, works offline.
2. **Step 2: Mini Hub** (`mini.html`)
   Run a free local hub on `127.0.0.1` for `base`, `staging`, and `live` settings, durable previews (local or Daytona), linked starters across apps, scoped agent keys, and approved delivery (Vercel, Fly, Unikraft, AWS SSM).
3. **Step 3: Shared Hub** (`hub.html`)
   Move current settings and their reasons to a hub teammates and CI can reach. Earlier revisions and delivery connections stay on the original hub.

## Key pages

- `index.html`: Overview, six core problems solved (3x2 grid + matching prompt table), Hero 1-line install, and interactive terminal demo.
- `first-look.html`: Three five-minute tasks (remember a setting, preview safely including Friday's live settings, reuse a starter across apps).
- `plugin.html`: Local change log, `/confighub:changes`, hooks, privacy/30-day transcript disclosure, and offline boundaries.
- `mini.html`: Local hub workflow, env checks, previews, and scoped keys.
- `hub.html`: Team governance, multi-app starters, and bridge to Kubernetes.
- `plugins.html`: Integrations (ConfigHub, nono sandbox, Daytona, Vercel, Fly, Unikraft, AWS SSM).
- `starters.html`: Interactive Plugin x Starter picker, Stripe/Supabase/Resend add-on starters, and K8s/GitOps/GPU graduation bridges (`#k8s-and-gpu`).
- `stories.html`: 25 audited first-use stories, 24 filterable field walkthroughs, and K8s/GPU graduation track (`#k8s-graduation`).
- `reference.html`: CLI commands, storage paths, and upstream repositories.
